QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_16

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah's firm is acquiring a 52% stake in the Investment Manager entity of Kaveri Opportunities Fund (Cat II), which would constitute a change in control. What is the correct regulatory action under Regulation 20(13) of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Post-facto intimation to SEBI within 30 days of the stake sale closing.
Prior approval from SEBI (the Board) must be obtained before the change in control is given effect.
Approval only from LPs holding 51% by value; SEBI notification is not required.
No approval required if the new controller is a SEBI-registered intermediary elsewhere.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Regulation 20(13) of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations requires PRIOR approval from SEBI for any change of Sponsor or Manager, or change in control of the AIF, Sponsor or Manager. 'Change in control' where the entity is a company includes the right to appoint majority directors or control policy decisions. **The Trap:** Post-facto intimation is wrong for a control change. LP consent (75%) is a separate workstream for the mandatory exit option to dissenters. Being a SEBI-registered intermediary elsewhere does NOT dispense with AIF-specific approval. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C identical. III-A/C (Compliance) tests change-of-control approval across broker, PMS, and AIF domains — the AIF-specific requirement is prior SEBI approval. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Factor a 60-90 day SEBI review into any M&A term sheet for AIF Manager acquisitions. Also line up the 75% LP consent in parallel — if you miss it, you trigger the mandatory exit to dissenters process.
